short: The largest battleship ever built by Germany, Bismarck was sunk in a massive British hunt after destroying HMS Hood.
full:
Commissioned in 1940, Bismarck represented the pinnacle of German surface naval power. Armed with 15-inch guns, the battleship was designed to raid Allied convoys in the Atlantic. During its only operational sortie in May 1941, it sank the pride of the Royal Navy, HMS Hood, at the Battle of the Denmark Strait.

The destruction of Hood sparked a relentless pursuit by the British Home Fleet. Crippled by a torpedo from a Swordfish biplane that jammed its steering gear, Bismarck was forced into a final surface engagement against battleships HMS King George V and HMS Rodney. Heavily battered, it was scuttled by its crew and sank, effectively ending Germany's surface threat in the Atlantic.
